text:
Marta: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to clarify Dedicated capacity SLA language and add tiny SDK examples for isolation tags. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4328
Kai: Reviewing now. Main ask: make SLA table explicit about preemption vs eviction semantics and what customers should expect for reserved pools.
Marta: Yep. Current copy is fuzzy around node reclamation vs tenant preemption. Want a plain sentence + table row.
Ram: I can add an autoscale policy snippet (YAML) and a minimal Terraform example showing reserved_pool, min/max, and isolation. Want both k8s and Terraform?
Marta: Both please. Keep k8s <8 lines. Terraform should include isolation = "tenant" and a short note about scheduling semantics.
Liam: Quick naming Q: "preemption" or "eviction"? Eng uses eviction; legal prefers preemption.
Sophia: Docs convention: first mention use "preemption (eviction)", then "preemption" afterwards. That keeps legal and eng happy.
Eve: FYI, the impact/runbook link is here: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-eviction — reference this from SLA.
DocsBot: link-checker: broken anchor detected -> docs/dedicated/#reserved-pools (404).
Kai: I'll fix the anchor and tighten SLA wording. For SDK snippets, do we want Python sync and Node?
Marta: Python sync + JS snippet. Keep each under 10 LOC.
Ram: Draft autoscale YAML:
Ram: ```yaml
scalePolicy:
  type: target_utilization
  target: 0.7
  windowSeconds: 60
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
```
Ram: Draft terraform snippet:
Ram: ```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "prod" {
  name         = "prod-reserved"
  gpu_type     = "a100"
  min_capacity = 2
  max_capacity = 20
  isolation    = "tenant"
}
```
Marta: Add a short inline note: "isolation = \"tenant\" implies nodes are scheduled for a single tenant; preemption only in out-of-contract emergency."
Kai: I'll add a bullet: "Tenant isolation: reserved nodes for single tenant; preemption only for emergency reclamation (see runbook)."
Liam: Also add a draft SLA table row: "Preemption: <1% monthly expected for reserved pools under normal ops (draft)" — mark as draft.
Sophia: I'll move SDK snippets under docs/examples/dedicated-sdk and create anchors to avoid link-check failures.
Eve: Suggest a 2-line canary rollback example in rollout section: route 5% to new model, fallback on latency/error threshold.
Marta: Agreed — add canary sample and explicit rollback trigger thresholds.
Kai: One more: state that latency SLOs only apply to committed capacity; burst capacity is best-effort. Don't promise SLOs during preemptible bursts.
Marta: Good call.
Ram: Pushing a follow-up commit with the Terraform + YAML snippets now.
Kai: Pushing wording changes and anchor fixes to the PR, will ping reviewers.
DocsBot: PR 4328 — status: changes requested (link-checks failing).
Marta: Thanks all. If you want to pair on SDK wording ping me in this thread. :thumbsup:
Sophia: I'll open a small follow-up PR for the example files after Kai lands wording changes (aiming in ~1h).
Liam: LGTM for structure. Also add a 1-line routing policy example: "latency-first" vs "cost-first" (sentence).
Marta: Noted, will add routing policy blurb.
Eve: Added a comment in the PR requesting telemetry/dashboard links to verify preemption rates.
Kai: Done — pushed wording + fixed anchor, re-running checks.
DocsBot: link-checker passed. CI: docs-build passed.
Marta: Great — we'll merge after Sophia's example PR lands.
Sophia: Opening example PR in ~1h.
Ram: My follow-up with snippets incoming in ~30m.
Marta: Thanks everyone, nice collaboration.
